bib.title: Context as an Environment: Programmatic Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: all 37 pages, 96,808 chars (extraction clean). Appendix D trajectories (pp. 18-37) were skimmed beyond D.1. No embedded instructions found.

TITLE: "Context as an Environment: Programmatic Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents". The user's brief calls it "Context Management as Code"; that phrase appears only in Figure 1 ("Scroll: context management as code"). The PDF is labelled "Technical Report."
AUTHORS: Yin Lin (Alibaba Group), Elaine Ang (Columbia University; internship at Alibaba), Erkang Zhu, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou (all Alibaba Group). Lin and Ang contributed equally.
VENUE/DATE: preprint, arXiv:2608.21690v1 [cs.AI], 21 Aug 2026. Code: github.com/niceIrene/QwenPaw (branch scroll-research).

MAIN CLAIM: Scroll keeps session history outside the prompt in an append-only SQLite Event Log. A persistent sandboxed Python kernel holds the working state, and only explicit `print` output enters the model's context. When the view exceeds its budget, stale spans are evicted from the view only. They stay verbatim in the log under a stable `seq` address. A tiered "eviction index" of model-written headlines, each tied to a `seq`, tells the agent what it can no longer see. Lossy compaction and write-time memory extraction decide what survives before the future need is known. Scroll defers that choice to query time.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (single run per task, Qwen3.8-Max backbone):
1. BEAM 10M: 73.1 judge score versus 68.0 for the best published system (Exabase M-1), a 5.1-point lead. Baselines are published numbers with different reader models and were not reproduced, so this is not a controlled comparison. Judge: Qwen3.6-flash, temperature 0.
2. LOCA, 128K to 256K environment length, same backbone and toolset. Accuracy drop from 128K to 256K:
   - Summarization agent: 86.7 to 65.3 (-21.4)
   - Retrieval/recall-tool agent: 88.0 to 66.7 (-21.3)
   - CodeAct agent: 89.3 to 85.3 (-4.0)
   - Scroll: 89.3 to 86.7 (-2.6)
   The "+37.4 over the best published agent" claim compares against MiniMax M3 + ReAct at 49.3, a different backbone. Sample size is not stated; the 128K figures are multiples of 1/75 (e.g. 89.3 = 67/75), which suggests about 75 tasks, but that is my inference, not stated.
3. Ablation on BEAM 10M (Qwen3.8-Max, thinking on):
   - Lossy summarization at ingestion, originals discarded: 19.9. The Figure 3 plot labels read 0.20, 0.66, 0.71, 0.73.
   - Without the REPL: -7.3 versus full Scroll.
   - Without the eviction index: -1.8, concentrated in preference following (89.1 vs 74.9).
4. LongMemEval S: 94.8, below Exabase M-1 at 96.4 (as printed in the Table 2 extraction) and Mastra OM at 94.9. LongMemEval M: 89.6 (Table 5). The median BEAM 10M query uses 105K input tokens, about 1% of the corpus.

QUOTES:
- p.2: "Unlike compaction, eviction changes only the view, never the underlying record: evicted events remain verbatim in the Event Log under their stable addresses"
- p.2: "Both are fundamentally lossy in the same way: the agent sees history only through the summary or the memory store, so any detail they fail to keep is out of reach—even if the raw log still exists on disk."
- p.5: "the procedure's one invariant is that everything it removes stays addressable."

DESIGN DETAILS FOR THE NOTE:
- Eviction order (Alg. 1, p.5): protect the active turn, recent tail and newest tool results. Fold completed tool payloads into `seq` pointers first. Evict whole spans only if the view is still over budget.
- Index rollup: each tier holds at most k blocks, so the index is O(k log_k n) blocks.
- Search is BM25, not embeddings, so it needs no index-time model calls.
- The model edits its own context by writing code. Table 1 gives four operations: LOCATE (`ms.search`), MATERIALIZE (`ms.expand`), COMPUTE (ordinary Python), EXPOSE (`print`).
- "Crash recovery" is not evaluated. The paper only describes durable storage, an event log that is read-only from the kernel, and a fail-closed sandbox. No kernel-restart or crash experiment is reported.

LIMITS:
- Baselines were not reproduced, and reader models differ across rows.
- Each task was run once, with no confidence intervals. Appendix A mentions "repeated runs" but gives no numbers.
- Only Qwen3.8-Max is the main backbone. Six backbones were tried and weaker ones fall far behind on LOCA at 256K: 86.7 for Qwen3.8-Max, 62.7 for GLM-5.2, 22.7 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Kimi-K2.7 scores 30.7/32.0.
- Weaker than baselines on summarization (70.5 vs 91.9), preference following (89.1 vs 97.5) and temporal reasoning (47.5 vs 58.8), because Scroll rebuilds condensed views per query. Multi-session reasoning is weak for all systems.
- LongMemEval degrades from S to M, mostly on multi-session and preference questions.
- Cost is reported only in tokens, not latency or dollars. For LongMemEval S and BEAM 10M it measures retrieval only.
- LOCA is scored on the final environment state with a rule-based verifier.
- Did not test: production compactors (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor), which are named only as "reportedly" compacting. The paper never compares against them, never tests an agent editing its own context natively, and has no real crash scenario.
- Future work: distilling the policy into small models via frontier traces.

BUILDS ON: CodeAct (Wang et al., 2024); Anthropic programmatic tool calling and code execution with MCP (2025); Recursive Language Models (Zhang, Kraska, Khattab, 2025); MemGPT (Packer et al., 2023); Lossless Context Management (Ehrlich and Blackman, Voltropy report, 2026); The Log is the Agent (Nakajima, arXiv 2026); ACON (Kang et al., 2025); AgentFold (Ye et al., 2025); MEM1 (Zhou et al., ICLR 2026); Memento (Kontonis et al., 2026); CoALA (Sumers et al., TMLR 2024). Benchmarks: LongMemEval (Wu et al., ICLR 2025), BEAM (Tavakoli et al., 2025), LOCA-bench (Zeng et al., 2026).

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 1 (p.3), the overview. It contrasts serialized-prompt management with the Event Log, kernel and tiered eviction index, including the `ms.expand(seq_lo, seq_hi)` recovery path. Figure 3 (p.9, ablation bars) is a good second choice for the "compaction loses detail" point.

PROBLEMS: none beyond text-layout noise in the figure and table extraction. The Table 2 bold markers are lost, so Exabase M-1 96.4/68.0 was read as "96.468.0".
